full_judgment:
2. Petitioner's Title Suit No. 21 of 1989 for permanent injunction was filed against the said Ministry, later on a prayer was made for mandatory injunction to restore possession of the disputed house to the plaintiff on the allegation that after filing of the suit the plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendants. The disputed house is situated at Mohammadpur, Dhaka, wherefrom the petitioner was threatened to be evicted by police force on the allegation that it was an abandoned property and hence the suit was filed which was dismissed by the trial court on 29-1-92. Trial Court's decree was affirmed in the other Appeal No. 80 of 1992 and the plaintiffs appeal was dismissed. The High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3519 of 1993 set aside the judgments and decree of the courts below and decreed the suit by its judgment and order dated 7-7-1997. The High Court Division also directed to restore possession of the suit property within 60 (Sixty) days from the date of judgment and order passed in the Civil Revision. 

 3. It is alleged in this application for drawing up contempt proceeding that the Government vis-a-vis the opposite parties are not delivering possession of the suit property to the plaintiff- petitioner although the said period has already expired. Where a court passes a decree for delivery of possession of a property to the plaintiff, the plaintiff is to put the decree in execution case for satisfaction of the decree. In this case we do not find that plaintiff-petitioner has taken such recourse. In a case where no such execution case is filed, the contempt petition avoiding such proceeding based on the ground of inaction on the part of the Government Officers and the defendant is misconceived. Since the decree was for giving delivery of possession, the plaintiff petitioner could take recourse as per Civil Procedure Code for getting possession of the suit property in a competent Court. Avoiding the same which is the proper course of law, this present application has been filed.
